sections.title: Form and leaves
sections.text: Rhamnus cathartica, common buckthorn, is a deciduous thorny shrub or small tree, usually about 5.5–9 m tall and 4.5–6 m wide. Its oval leaves have finely toothed margins and often show curved veins.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small greenish flowers appear in the leaf axils. Female plants produce clusters of round black berries, about 6–10 mm across, each containing several seeds.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The berries and other parts have purgative effects and can cause illness if eaten; they are not food. The illustration's ripe black fruit and thorn-tipped branches fit this species.
